subject: Stress SLO alignment + prompt curation and reproducibility ops
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@fountainretail.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.example.com
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@fountainretail.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fountain: follow-up on perf targets & benchmark plan

Diego / team,

Thanks again for the demo today — appreciate the concise walkthrough of routing and fallback behavior. A couple of immediate items we need to lock down so we can align our SLOs with engineering:

- Target P95 latency for a 1,024-token streaming response under 1 concurrent request: is 120ms per token realistic on your hosted profile?
- Expected throughput at sustained 400 concurrent users (mix of short chatbot + longer content generations) — ballpark TPS and how batching affects latency
- Streaming specifics: we require early-token delivery within 200ms of first token for 80% of requests when using continuous streaming + function-calls

We also want the benchmark methodology your team will run so we can validate results: prompt sets, randomization, KV-cache warm/cold definitions, reproducibility steps, and any non-determinism notes (sampling, temperature).

Can you send a short plan and any artifacts we can run locally against our harness? We want to begin an internal validation run next week.

Best,
Elaine Park
Director, Platform Engineering
Fountain Retail

--
Attachment: N/A
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.example.com
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@fountainretail.com>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@fountainretail.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fountain: follow-up on perf targets & benchmark plan

Elaine — thanks for the crisp list. Quick answers, then a proposed artifact bundle we can share: 

- P95 per-token: for hosted thin profiles with streaming enabled we typically see ~90–130ms per token at 1 concurrent request, depending on model context size and quantization. 120ms is within expected range for the model variant we demoed.
- Sustained 400 concurrent users: this is primarily a capacity planning question (batching, arrival distribution). On Dedicated pools we’d expect to sustain your workload with target latency SLOs; for hosted, we’ll propose a run that simulates your mix and reports both median/T95/T99 and the per-token streaming tail.
- Streaming early-token delivery: we can instrument a hook that captures first-byte latency; Redwood can measure percentiles across runs. 200ms for 80% is achievable with warmed KV cache and proper batching constraints; cold-cache worst-case will be higher.

Attached I’m sharing a compiled artifact list and a short run plan (summary). I’ll loop in Marissa and Ben internally to provide the harness bundle and the reproducibility checklist.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll drop the harness bundle by EOD PT (prompt sets + runner config).
2) You spin up a validation run using the included matrix; we pair on a quick call if results diverge.
3) If needed, we propose a dedicated qualification run on a Reserved pool for an apples-to-apples.

- Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments referenced: benchmark-artifact-list.txt
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.example.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, ben_carter@redwood.example.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.example.com
Date: Sat, 8 May 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Fountain validation bundle — ask list

Marissa / Ben / Priyom,

Elaine asked for a lightweight, reproducible harness and prompt set they can run locally next week. Please prioritize the following artifacts and clarifications:

1) prompt-set-v2.jsonl — canonical prompt families (chat short, chat long, instruction >1k tokens) with seed annotations and expected output markers for exact-match checks.
2) latency-sample-matrix.csv — arrival patterns (poisson, burst, steady) and concurrency mix to reproduce their 400-user scenario.
3) redwood-benchmark-groups.pdf — short doc describing warm/cold-KV definitions, sampling settings (temperature/top-p), and kernel/quantization profile used.
4) FR-bench-harness-v1.zip — a runner that can (a) replay the prompt set, (b) capture first-byte and per-token timestamps, (c) seed RNG where applicable and checksum outputs. Include README with reproducibility steps and a minimal Dockerfile.

Specific asks: for the harness, ensure there is a toggle: deterministic-mode (fixed RNG, greedy decoding) vs production-mode (sampling). Record non-deterministic elements in the run metadata. Also add a small script to compute the first-byte latency metric for streaming.

Target: have the bundle ready by EOD PT today so Dieg o can send to the customer. If there are tradeoffs (size, secrets), flag them.

Thanks — Diego

--
(This is an internal note — do not forward external until artifacts are sanitized.)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.example.com
Date: Sat, 8 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Fountain validation bundle — ask list

Diego / team — attaching the initial bundle and a short runbook. Key points to call out for Fountain: 

- prompt-set-v2.jsonl (attached): 180 prompts, split into 3 families. Each file has a seed and an expected token-length bracket.
- prompt randomization: we use block-randomization by family to keep latency signal stable across runs.
- determinism: deterministic-mode pins RNG and uses greedy decode (we include checksums). production-mode will be non-deterministic; we include run-diff tooling.
- first-byte capture: harness emits a streaming-first-byte.csv with timestamps for request-start, first-byte, and each token.
- quantization profile: qa-8q4f (documented in redwood-benchmark-groups.pdf). We list kernel overrides and expected memory footprint.

Attachments: FR-bench-harness-v1.zip (runner + Dockerfile), prompt-set-v2.jsonl, latency-sample-matrix.csv, redwood-benchmark-groups.pdf

Let me know if you want a smaller smoke pack for an initial sanity run (I can produce a 12-prompt quickset).

— Ben
Performance Engineering
Redwood Inference

--

Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@fountainretail.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, ben_carter@redwood.example.com
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fountain: follow-up on perf targets & benchmark plan

Elaine — attaching the bundle Ben prepared (see list below). Quick summary of what to expect and how to run: 

What we attached: FR-bench-harness-v1.zip (runner + Dockerfile), prompt-set-v2.jsonl (canonical prompts), latency-sample-matrix.csv (arrival/concurrency patterns), redwood-benchmark-groups.pdf (methodology & config).

Run notes:
- Start in deterministic-mode on a small smoke set (12 prompts) to validate plumbing.
- Then run production-mode with their arrival pattern (400 concurrent mix) for 30 minutes to capture steady-state metrics.
- We recommend two passes: cold-cache (fresh process) and warm-cache (after 15m warm-up). The harness marks each request with cache_state tag.

Deliverables we’ll provide after your run: raw run CSVs, aggregated percentile table (P50/P95/P99) for both first-byte and per-token latencies, and a short variance note that explains any run-to-run drift. If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute triage call on Wednesday to go over results.

Proposed timeline: your validation run Mon/Tue, Redwood triage Wed, dedicated qualification (reserved pool) — optional — the following week.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

--

Diego / team — got the bundle, thanks. Samir and I will run the deterministic smoke on Monday morning and the scaled production-mode run Tuesday afternoon. A couple of clarifications before we kick off: 

1) For the 400-user arrival matrix — do you have a recommended request rate per second we should target (TPS)? We’ll follow the matrix but want a guidance number to sanity-check our generator.
2) If we see sustained P95 per-token above 150ms in the production-mode run, should we open a ticket with Redwood or schedule the reserved qualification immediately?

We’ll share raw CSVs to the Drive link and set the triage call for Wednesday 15:00 PT if that works for your team.

Regards,
Elaine Park
